articles.title: Jon Jones finally remembers longtime “frenemy” Daniel Cormier after struggling through hilarious pizza challenge
articles.summary: Jon Jones has once again brought Daniel Cormier into the spotlight, but this time in a much lighter way.
articles.body: Jon Jones has once again brought Daniel Cormier into the spotlight, but this time in a much lighter way. The former UFC champion appeared to remember his longtime rival while taking part in a pizza challenge. After only a few bites, Jones joked that he needed help from Cormier to get through the challenge.Jones and Cormier shared one of the fiercest rivalries in UFC history. Their rivalry featured heated exchanges, a famous media-day brawl and two championship fights. While their relationship has become more cordial over the years, Cormier has made it clear that the two are not friends. Jones’ latest comment, however, showed that their rivalry can still produce plenty of laughs.Jon Jones calls on Daniel Cormier for help during pizza challengeDuring a recent pizza challenge, Jon Jones appeared to struggle after eating only a few bites. The moment prompted him to jokingly call on the man who was once his biggest rival inside the UFC.“I have never wanted to see Daniel Cormier more than I want to see him right now. Tag in brother”, he said.The comment became a funny reminder of one of the most famous rivalries in MMA history. Jones and Cormier spent years trading verbal shots and building intense animosity before finally settling their differences inside the Octagon.Their first fight took place at UFC 182 in January 2015. Jones entered the bout as the UFC light heavyweight champion and defeated Cormier by unanimous decision. The fight was the culmination of years of tension between the two fighters.The rivalry became even more heated before their first meeting. In 2014, Jones and Cormier were involved in a wild confrontation during a UFC 178 media event. The two fighters got into a physical altercation during their face-off, with the incident spilling from the stage into the lobby.They eventually met again at UFC 214 in July 2017. Jones stopped Cormier with a third-round head kick and punches. However, the result was later overturned to a No Contest after Jones tested positive for turinabol. Jones was stripped of the title, while Cormier was reinstated as champion.Despite the bitter history, their relationship has changed over time. The two have been able to appear together professionally and interact without the same level of hostility that defined their rivalry during their fighting careers.However, Cormier has previously explained that he does not consider Jones a friend. Their history remains too complicated, particularly because of the controversies surrounding Jones’ drug-testing history.Cormier retired from MMA in 2020 after completing his trilogy with Stipe Miocic. Jones later moved to heavyweight and became the UFC heavyweight champion.Their competitive careers have taken them in different directions. Yet moments like Jones’ pizza challenge comment show that Cormier remains a familiar name in his mind. articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Tickets priced up to £13,000 for all-British showdown sell out in one hour
articles.summary: Tickets for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium sells out in just one hour.
articles.body:
Tickets for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium have sold out in just one hour.

Fury and Joshua will meet on a bill that begins on 11 December but they are not expected to fight until the early hours of 12 December.

The highest-priced tickets were available at £13,128, including booking fees, with the lowest at £88.50.

The all-British heavyweight contest, which will be broadcast globally on Netflix, was announced in September and around 80,000 tickets went on sale at 12:00 BST on Friday.

Just minutes after the tickets went on sale more than 500,000 people were waiting in the online queue.

Tickets quickly began emerging on resale websites, with ringside VIP seats being advertised for £73,645, while upper tier seats were available for £425.

Ringwalks are expected to start around 01:00 GMT on Saturday 12 December, following a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 03:30.

The event is being promoted as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and UFC chief Dana White.

Organisers are yet to confirm any of the undercard fights.

Joshua, 36, and Fury, 38 - both former two-time world champions - signed contracts for the bout earlier this year, but the date and venue had yet to be confirmed.

London's Wembley Stadium and New York's Madison Square Garden were the frontrunners to stage the fight, but both presented issues before Cardiff emerged as an alternative.

The Principality Stadium has hosted late-night boxing before, including Joe Calzaghe's fight with Mikkel Kessler in November 2007, which began at 01:00 GMT.

Ricky Hatton's victory over Kostya Tszyu at Manchester's MEN Arena in 2005 began at about 02:00 local time, allowing US broadcaster Showtime to show the fight on Saturday evening.

Just 11 days ago, there was uncertainty over whether the fight would even take place due to a dispute over the role of UFC chief White in the promotion of the event.

Broadcaster Netflix said Alalshikh's The Ring and White would collaborate to promote the event, but Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn said his fighter's contract prevented White from having a promotional role.

The British rivals finally met at a news conference on 30 September to begin the build-up to one of the most anticipated fights in British history.

Fury and Joshua are reported to be sharing a purse worth close to $200m (£151m)

articles.title: Who is Plinio Cruz? All about Alex Pereira’s coach set to make boxing debut against Gary Olive
articles.summary: Plinio Cruz is best known as the head coach and translator of UFC superstar Alex Pereira.
articles.body: Plinio Cruz is best known as the head coach and translator of UFC superstar Alex Pereira. The Brazilian-American mixed martial arts coach has played an important role in Pereira’s rise to the top of the sport. He has also worked with several other fighters, including former UFC light heavyweight champion Glover Teixeira. Cruz has built a reputation for his coaching skills, martial arts knowledge, and close relationship with Pereira.Cruz is now preparing for a new challenge outside mixed martial arts. He is set to make his boxing debut against Gary Olive at a Misfits Boxing event in London on October 10, 2026. The bout was arranged after original opponent Chase DeMoor withdrew because of an eye injury.Who is Plinio CruzPlinio Cruz has established himself as a respected coach in the mixed martial arts community. He serves as the head coach at Cruz Mixed Martial Arts, also known as Cruz MMA. His work involves preparing fighters for competition and helping them develop their skills inside the cage.Cruz is particularly recognised for his partnership with Alex Pereira. He has coached the Brazilian star throughout his rise in combat sports and has also helped him communicate with English-speaking audiences. His role as Pereira’s translator has made him a familiar face to UFC fans.The coach has also worked with Glover Teixeira, a former UFC light heavyweight champion. In addition, he has trained rising heavyweight fighter King Edokpolo. His experience working with fighters at different stages of their careers has helped establish his reputation in the sport.Cruz’s achievements have also received recognition at the World MMA Awards. He won the Coach of the Year award at the 16th edition of the ceremony, highlighting his contribution to the sport.Beyond coaching, Cruz has a background as a professional mixed martial artist. He competed in the heavyweight division and reportedly finished his professional career with an 8-9 record. He is also a former Cage Fury Fighting Championships heavyweight champion and competed under promotions such as Bellator and M-1 Global.Cruz has extensive martial arts experience. He holds a third-degree black belt in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and a second-degree black belt in judo. These qualifications reflect his experience in grappling and other traditional martial arts disciplines.Cruz is now stepping into the boxing ring for the first time as a competitor. He was initially scheduled to face Chase DeMoor, the Misfits Boxing heavyweight champion, on October 10 at the Copper Box Arena in London. However, DeMoor withdrew after suffering an eye injury.The promotion subsequently announced that Gary Olive, DeMoor’s coach, would replace him. The contest was described as a “Battle of the Coaches.”Cruz’s boxing debut gives the experienced MMA coach an opportunity to test himself in a different combat sport. articles.title: La campeona olímpica y mujer hiperandrógina Imane Khelif retoma su paso al profesionalismo
articles.standfirst: Debutará por fin en diciembre en París tras suspenderse su debut en abril por una lesión
articles.summary: Debutará por fin en diciembre en París tras suspenderse su debut en abril por una lesión
articles.body: La boxeadora argelina Imane Khelif, posiblemente el oro olímpico más polémico de París 2024 por su condición de mujer hiperandrógina, ha retomado su idea de pasarse al profesionalismo tras un primer intento frustado por una lesión. La idea es que debute en diciembre en París frente a un rival aún por determinar. Así lo ha revelado el diario L'Equipe en un artículo en el que relata que en esta nueva aventura va de la mano del promotor Yacin Berrabah. El combate sería el 11 de diciembre en el Dôme de París o el 17 en el Clichy Hall (Hauts-de-Seine), aunque hasta el 5 de noviembre no se desvelarán más detalles. La campeona olímpica en la categoría de -66 kg firmó inicialmente con Brahim Asloum, el hombre que derrotó a Rafael Lozano en la final olímpica del peso minimosca (-48 kilos) en Sidney 2000, para convertirse en profesional e iba a debutar el 23 de abril en la Salle Wagram de París, pero una lesión en el hombro obligó a cancelar este combate. Tras este intento frustrado, la argelina ha puesto su carrera en manos de Yacin Berrabah, un experimentado promotor que organiza tanto veladas de boxeo como de kickboxing. "El director ejecutivo de su principal patrocinador, la marca argelina de cosméticos Belnco, me contactó para conseguirle una pelea", explicó Berrabah a L'Equipe. "Conocí a Imane y tengo un acuerdo con ella para sus tres primeras peleas. Estoy buscando una televisión (su pelea podría transmitirse por Twitch) y patrocinadores, pero no quiero interponerme en su camino, y si algún promotor extranjero importante está interesado en representarla, será bienvenido", añadió este ex campeón del mundo de kickboxing. Imane Khelif, de 26 años, sueña con defender su oro olímpico en Los Ángeles 2028 pero de momento no cuenta con el beneplácito de World Boxing, organismo que asumió provisionalmente la gestión del boxeo olímpico y que ya le impidió participar en el Mundial de septiembre de 2025 en Liverpool tras negarse a someterse a las pruebas genéticas de sexo para verificar la ausencia del gen SRY (típico del cromosoma Y). La argelina ha declarado que no se niega a pasar pruebas genéticas siempre que sean bajo el amparo del Comité Olímpico Internacional y ha presentando un recurso ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) para recuperar sus derechos deportivos.

articles.title: Anthony Cacace vs Nick Ball: Vasiliy Lomachenko interest not a distraction for world champion
articles.summary: WBA super-featherweight champion Anthony Cacace is not prepared to allow suggestions of a showdown with Vasiliy Lomachenko distract him as he prepares to take on Nick Ball.
articles.body:
WBA super-featherweight champion Anthony Cacace is not prepared to allow suggestions of a showdown with Vasiliy Lomachenko distract him as he prepares to take on Nick Ball.

The 37-year-old makes his maiden defence of the title against Liverpool's former WBA featherweight champion Ball at the recently renamed O2 Belfast on Saturday, 19 December.

The WBA has already indicated the winner must face Russia's Elnur Samedov next, but the returning Lomachenko is reported to be keen too, according to ESPN's Brian Custer. , external

Should that come to pass, it would represent the realisation of a dream for Cacace, but his immediate gaze remains firmly fixed on Ball.

"I'm not really thinking about that just now, I just kind of want to focus fully on Nick Ball and this fight coming up," he insisted.

"I woke up to them type of things [Lomachenko interest] going to myself, 'what?'. To see that type of stuff blows my mind but it's one of those things and I'm just super grateful for it all.

"I remember putting a tweet out in 2012 calling out Lomachenko, so if that fight ever materialises, I'll get that tweet sorted."

The last time Cacace boxed in the arena was in 2023, out-pointing Damian Wrzesinski over 12 rounds on the undercard of Luis Alberto Lopez's defeat of Michael Conlan in an IBF featherweight title defence.

Sandwiched between those two bouts was a victory for Ball over Ludumo Lamati, a fight that ended in worrying scenes with the South African suffering a stroke in the ring when stopped in the final round, but has since made a full recovery.

The Liverpudlian "didn't even know that" he and Cacace shared that undercard but was more than happy to return to Belfast for this opportunity.

Three successful defences would follow, but in February of this year, it all unravelled in the final round against Brandon Figueroa when he was dropped twice and then stopped, suffering his first career loss in his 25th professional bout.

"It was a good fight, back and forth for 12 rounds and he caught me with a good shot in the last round," Ball reflected.

"He threw an overhand left counter as I was throwing, so that's what happened. It's boxing, it's part of the game."

A bundle of aggression, Ball brings a relentless style but will concede considerable height and reach advantages to Cacace in what his his first step up into the super-featherweight division with the opportunity to become a two-weight champion "something special".

The move up was prompted by this opportunity alone, but feels he will be "stronger, more comfortable" and is not concerned about fighting a much bigger man.

"All fights are challenging," he countered.

"The reach and the size advantage [for opponents], I've been doing that my whole career, so that's nothing new to me."

'Dream come true' for Cacace to defend at home

In his 26-fight career, Cacace has boxed in his native Belfast on just five occasions, so to headline in his home city for the first time in a world title defence is "a dream come true".

He has been riding the crest of a wave since winning his first world title in 2024 when he stopped Joe Cordina for the IBF version in Saudi Arabia - and there has been no looking back.

Wins over Josh Warrington and Leigh Wood - which came after vacating the title - would set him up for a shot at then WBA-holder James 'Jazza' Dickens earlier this year and it proved another night of glory for a man whose career had previously been confined to the shadows.

"I always wanted to come back and have one big show," he said. "It's a dream come true. I never believed I'd be in this situation, but here I am.

"I'm just expecting the usual Nick Ball, [he'll] come forward with aggression.

"I feel like I can do it all. I can deal with him and deal with those styles for 20-plus years, so it's just going to be another fight, another good fight and hopefully a good show for Belfast."
